From 9153e6b7c85edbc89e874e5c83f86217c53dcfaf Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2018 09:10:27 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/execlists: Use a locked clear_bit() for
 synchronisation with interrupt

We were relying on the uncached reads when processing the CSB to provide
ourselves with the serialisation with the interrupt handler (so we could
detect new interrupts in the middle of processing the old one). However,
in commit 767a983ab255 ("drm/i915/execlists: Read the context-status HEAD
from the HWSP") those uncached reads were eliminated (on one path at
least) and along with them our serialisation. The result is that we
would very rarely miss notification of a new interrupt and leave a
context-switch unprocessed, hanging the GPU.

Fixes: 767a983ab255 ("drm/i915/execlists: Read the context-status HEAD from the HWSP")
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Michel Thierry <michel.thierry@intel.com>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Cc: Mika Kuoppala <mika.kuoppala@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Mika Kuoppala <mika.kuoppala@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Michel Thierry <michel.thierry@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20180321091027.21034-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

index 53f1c009ed7b..67b6a0f658d6 100644

+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_lrc.c
@@ -831,7 +831,8 @@ static void execlists_submission_tasklet(unsigned long data)

-	/* We can skip acquiring intel_runtime_pm_get() here as it was taken
+	/*
+	 * We can skip acquiring intel_runtime_pm_get() here as it was taken
 	 * on our behalf by the request (see i915_gem_mark_busy()) and it will
 	 * not be relinquished until the device is idle (see
 	 * i915_gem_idle_work_handler()). As a precaution, we make sure
@@ -840,7 +841,8 @@ static void execlists_submission_tasklet(unsigned long data)
 	 */
 	GEM_BUG_ON(!dev_priv->gt.awake);
 
-	/* Prefer doing test_and_clear_bit() as a two stage operation to avoid
+	/*
+	 * Prefer doing test_and_clear_bit() as a two stage operation to avoid
 	 * imposing the cost of a locked atomic transaction when submitting a
 	 * new request (outside of the context-switch interrupt).
 	 */
@@ -856,17 +858,10 @@ static void execlists_submission_tasklet(unsigned long data)
 			execlists->csb_head = -1; /* force mmio read of CSB ptrs */
 		}
 
-		/* The write will be ordered by the uncached read (itself
-		 * a memory barrier), so we do not need another in the form
-		 * of a locked instruction. The race between the interrupt
-		 * handler and the split test/clear is harmless as we order
-		 * our clear before the CSB read. If the interrupt arrived
-		 * first between the test and the clear, we read the updated
-		 * CSB and clear the bit. If the interrupt arrives as we read
-		 * the CSB or later (i.e. after we had cleared the bit) the bit
-		 * is set and we do a new loop.

2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_lrc.c`**
1. **Comment Updates**: Several comments were modified for clarity, particularly around the rationale for skipping certain operations and the behavior of the `test_and_clear_bit()` function.
2. **Bit Clearing Logic**: The method of clearing the interrupt bit was changed:
   - The original code used `__clear_bit(ENGINE_IRQ_EXECLIST, &engine->irq_posted);` which did not ensure proper synchronization with the interrupt handler.
   - This was replaced with `clear_bit(ENGINE_IRQ_EXECLIST, &engine->irq_posted);` followed by a memory barrier `smp_mb__after_atomic();` to ensure that the bit is cleared before reading the context-status buffer (CSB), thus improving synchronization and preventing missed interrupts.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `intel_lrc.c` file are directly related to addressing a bug introduced in a previous commit (767a983ab255). The original reliance on uncached reads for synchronization was removed in that commit, leading to potential missed interrupts and unprocessed context switches. The changes made in this patch reintroduce a more reliable synchronization mechanism by using a locked `clear_bit()` operation, ensuring that the clearing of the interrupt bit occurs before reading the CSB. This relationship highlights the importance of proper synchronization in interrupt handling to maintain GPU stability and performance.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
__clear_bit(ENGINE_IRQ_EXECLIST, &engine->irq_posted);
```
```c
/* The write will be ordered by the uncached read (itself
 * a memory barrier), so we do not need another in the form
 * of a locked instruction. */
```
```c
/* We were relying on the uncached reads when processing the CSB to provide
 * ourselves with the serialisation with the interrupt handler */
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the removal of uncached reads eliminated the necessary serialization with the interrupt handler. This means that when the `__clear_bit` operation is performed, there is no guarantee that the interrupt handler has completed processing, leading to a race condition where new interrupts could be missed while processing existing ones.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
clear_bit(ENGINE_IRQ_EXECLIST, &engine->irq_posted);
```
```c
smp_mb__after_atomic();
```
Reason:
The fix involves using `clear_bit` instead of `__clear_bit`, which ensures that the operation is performed in a locked manner, providing the necessary synchronization with the interrupt handler. The addition of `smp_mb__after_atomic()` acts as a memory barrier, ensuring that all memory operations before this point are completed before any subsequent operations, thus preventing the race condition and ensuring that new interrupts are not missed.
